pages.title: Zeolite Catalyst
pages.text: An aluminosilicate crystal riddled with channels the width of a single molecule. Anything that fits inside is held in exactly the right pose to react, so reactions that would idle in open air happen in a blink. It is light, chalky and faintly gritty, like pumice that remembers being a mineral.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Clay and quartz dissolved in supercritical solvent recrystallised into a sponge of perfect pores. With a pinch of Cherenkov quartz as a template the channels came out uniform, and molecules small enough to enter came out changed.
